defaultAnswers.answer: This result identifies bounding box locations where the optical model detected visible floating-waste objects above confidence threshold 0.25. It reflects visible surface objects captured in this photograph. It does not measure chemical water quality, pathogens, or drinking-water safety.

The model detected {count} visible floating-waste candidates in this image at confidence ≥ 0.25. Detections were predicted using the unified YOLO26s-P2 detector for the single class 'floating_waste'. Inspect individual boxes on the photo to review candidate locations.

Visible floating debris indicates surface plastic or municipal waste accumulation at this photographed location, but optical detection alone cannot measure chemical contamination, dissolved toxins, or overall water safety. Physical sampling and laboratory testing are required for water quality assessment.

Review each bounding box on the image to verify detections against possible water surface reflections, wave crests, or vegetation. You can also adjust the confidence threshold slider to inspect higher or lower confidence candidate boxes.

defaultAnswers.answer: At the active confidence threshold of 0.25, the model detected {count} visible floating-waste objects in this image. Detections were made using the YOLO26s-P2 unified detector.

Reliability depends on the water condition and confidence threshold. On the TUD-GV and IWHR evaluation sets, detections in the 0.75–1.00 band achieved 88–97% precision, while detections below 0.25 had precision under 45%. This image is categorized as '{imageCheck}' to evaluation benchmarks.

Results may be uncertain due to domain shift: differences in water turbidity, sun reflection glare, waves, or camera distance that differ from the two training datasets. In addition, raw confidence scores are uncalibrated and should not be interpreted as exact probabilities.

facts.knownFalsePositives: Wave crest reflections, sun glints, floating organic foam

defaultAnswers.answer: The model has only one class ('floating waste'). It does not identify material types (such as whether an item is PET plastic, glass, or aluminum), does not compute pollution severity scores, cannot estimate submerged depth, and does not establish safety risks.
